status.scope_reason: The company provides a digital trade documentation and transaction network that enables the exchange of electronic bills of lading and structured presentations for trade finance.
status.evidence: According to WaveBL's official platform documentation, it operates a blockchain-based digital network for electronic bills of lading and bank presentations in trade finance.

claims.claim: The company reports its platform enables structured bank presentations for letters of credit and collection transactions via network integrations with partners like TradeWaltz, and supported a non-bank trade finance transaction with Capital4Trade using its eBL with decentralized finance (DeFi) liquidity.

OGYDocs Inc. (operating its WaveBL platform) implemented the Digital Container Shipping Association (DCSA) Standard Annex for eBL Platform Interoperability v.2 in June 2026, enabling its blockchain ecosystem to exchange electronic bills of lading multilaterally across other approved systems like CargoX, edoxOnline, TradeGo, and eTEU.
claims.note: The implementation of DCSA Standard Annex for eBL Platform Interoperability v.2 specifically in June 2026, and multilateral cross-platform exchange with TradeGo and eTEU, is unverified by published sources.

claims.claim: The company completed a proof of value network connectivity project with Swift and five global banking institutions in late 2024, demonstrating secure transfers of structured bank presentations and electronic bills of lading through Swift's FileAct file transfer service.

The company offers integrated connectivity to global core banking frameworks via third-party technical integrations with trade finance software providers, explicitly partner technology platforms Temenos and Surecomp.
claims.source: WaveBL Bank Use Case and Partner Documentation (Temenos and Surecomp RIVO)

claims.claim: The company reports in July 2026 that it raised $6 million to expand its trade finance capabilities and strengthen its AI-powered services.
claims.corrected: The company reports in June 2023 that it raised $26 million to expand its trade finance capabilities and strengthen its services.
claims.source: WaveBL Official Series B Press Release (June 2023) / PitchBook / Tracxn Funding Records

claims.claim: The company reports that its core blockchain-based electronic bill of lading (eBL) network has been expanded through its "Digital Envelope" solution to securely bundle all transaction documents (such as Commercial Invoices and Packing Lists) alongside AI-driven validation, real-time error detection, and compliance checking tools.
claims.corrected: The company reports that its core blockchain-based electronic bill of lading (eBL) network has been expanded through its "Wave Pouch" solution to securely bundle all transaction documents (such as Commercial Invoices and Packing Lists) alongside AI-driven validation, real-time error detection, and compliance checking tools.

claims.claim: Barclays Bank signed an agreement with OGYDocs (Wave) in 2015 to leverage its blockchain application within Barclays Corporate Bank, executing its first live blockchain trade finance transaction in 2016.
The company reports that its digital courier and electronic bill of lading platform is used across more than 100 countries globally.
OGYDocs Inc. (operating as WaveBL) has raised a total of $15.2 million in venture funding, completing early-stage funding rounds that include a Series A in 2019 and a Series B in 2021.
claims.corrected: OGYDocs Inc. (operating as WaveBL) has raised a total of $37 million in venture funding, completing early-stage funding rounds that include a Series A in 2019 and a Series B in 2021.

claims.claim: The company has secured backing from strategic and institutional investors, including ZIM Integrated Shipping Services, Contour Venture Partners, NewRoad Capital Partners, and angel investors such as Jeroen Bertrams.

The company reports that its platform, operating under the WaveBL brand, has achieved a 65% share of the global electronic bill of lading (eBL) market, processing more than 500,000 eBL issuances in 2025.
claims.source: WaveBL LinkedIn End of Year Report / Company Website

claims.claim: The network connects users across more than 100 countries, including 7 of the world's top 12 ocean carriers, 25+ freight forwarders, and banking institutions like Lloyds Bank, Federal Bank, Emirates NBD Bank, U.S. Bank, and Bank Mizrahi.
claims.source: WaveBL Press Releases / Official Case Studies
